messages.author: 3c18110a9f0f27e6
messages.subject: Nested tabsets?
parts:
Is it not possible in Shiny to have tabsets nested inside one another, so as to create a hierarchical structure of pages?  More generally: Is it possible in Shiny to nest any page type inside of another one?

I have found that the side bar on pageWithSidebar() takes up more of the screen than I would like.  In particular, I would like to include a tabset with several tabs. However, with side bar taking up so much horizontal real estate, there is not enough room on the screen for an orderly and clear presentation.

In response, I have been working to create an app which will have two tiers of tabsets.  All seemed to be going well. But I have started to encounter some flaky behavior: a widget that is supposed to only show up under some conditions is showing up all the time. 

Before delving further down the rabbit hole of debugging, I thought I would check to see if the problems may be associated with the nesting structure itself.

The structure I'm working on looks (in stripped-down form) as follows:

shinyUI(
  bootstrapPage(

    h1("Welcome to My Web App"), 

    tabsetPanel(id="openTab",

      tabPanel("Welcome", value='welcome', "We hope you enjoy your stay."),

              tabPanel("Your Data", value='data',

                 #  Here we create a second row of tabsets underneath the first row
                 tabsetPanel(id="dataTab",
          
                   tabPanel("Choose a dataset", value='chooseData',
                 selectInput("dataset", "Choose an example dataset:",
                    list("Cylinders" = "cyl",
                           "Transmission" = "am", 
                           "Gears" = "gear")
                 ),      # Close selectInput()
                  ),         # Close second-level tabPanel()

                 # Open another second-level tab, subordinated to the top-level "Data" tab
                 tabPanel("Examine your data", value='viewData', 
                     verbatimTextOutput("dataSummary"),
                     tableOutput("tableOfData")
                )  # Close secondary tabPanel() "viewData"
               )   # Close secondary tabsetPanel() "dataTab"
             )    # Close top-level tabPanel() "Your Data"
    )))  # Close top-level tabset(), close bootstrapPage(), close shinyUI()
                             

I'm not at this point looking for help debugging this code: this isn't the actual code, just a stripped down example. I'm just looking for insight into Shiny's capabilities to handle nested page types.  I am aware that it it is possible to create the user interface in HTML, instead of using Shiny's ui facilities. I would prefer to avoid going that route, at least for now.

My thanks for any insight.

Cheers,

Arthur

Please take a look at twitter bootstrap: this is what the UI is built using, and is supremely capable.  You should have no problem extending your layout using bootstrap features.

pageWithSidebar is simply a recipe using bootstrap.

-Alex Brown

Can't help you on the page layout side but if you find out how to adjust things like the width of the sidebar let us know. A few Gist's on how this works from those in-the-know would be awesome (e.g., how make the selectInput with multiple = TRUE longer?).

I am not sure about any page but what you are trying seems fine as far as I can tell. You might not need the ',' at the end of the following bit of code in your example. You can get strange results behavior if the )'s and ,'s are not just right.

selectInput("dataset", "Choose an example dataset:",
                    list("Cylinders" = "cyl",
                           "Transmission" = "am", 
                           "Gears" = "gear")
                 ),      # Close selectInput()

@Alex: If I can't fix the snag myself, I will take you up on your kind offer.  Thanks for your helpful feedback!

@Vincent:  You are absolutely right about "shouldn't" != "won't" :) . (Have you ever asked for directions and been told "Ya can't miss it"? Though I'm not generally superstitious, I believe that particular phrase has the hexing power to warp space-time so as to make accurate navigation impossible.) 

I've become quite familiar with the comma conundrum. In my experience misplaced commas don't lead to strange behavior: they generate no behavior at all, a.k.a. a crash. 

I suspect that implementing more flexible features such as you describe will involve someone stepping up to code new Shiny functions based on Twitter Bootstrap, e.g., pageWithSidebar() v. 2.0. Such work lies outside my own current skill set, however (as evidenced by my semi-newbie question).
 
Thanks again to you both.

- Arthur
